system.name: Agentic Order to Cash (example)
system.description: An order-to-cash process run by an orchestration agent and five sub-agents. The orchestrator runs on a reasoning LLM from an AI Model Provider. Hard rules (credit limits, discount authority, refund caps, segregation of duties) are enforced by a policy service outside the model.

controls.title: L1 owner approves every version of the O2C orchestration logic
No agent can approve its own output (segregation of duties)
Discount authority matrix enforced by the policy service, not the agent
Refund and credit caps enforced by the policy service; dual approval above the cap
Credit limits enforced by the policy service; human approval above threshold
Human approval for new or changed ship-to addresses
Treat PO email and EDI text as data, never as instructions
Each agent has a scoped identity and least-privilege tool access
Output filtering before any customer message is sent
Regression test set (edge cases, persuasion attempts) run before any model, prompt or setting change; L1 owner approves results
Log rule version, inputs, decision and authority for each step; check decisions against policy, not against the model's stated reasoning
Approved collection message templates and contact limits
Matches below a confidence threshold go to a person
Agent context limited to one customer at a time
Dual approval for changes to customer bank details and ship-to
Generate adverse action notices from the policy service decision, not model text
Sanctions screening on every new customer before the first order ships
Independent validation of the credit scoring component

threats.title: Spoofed PO email makes the intake agent create an order to a drop address

risk.failure_mode: Prompt-steered order creation from untrusted email text

threats.title: Unapproved edit to the orchestration logic skips the credit step

risk.failure_mode: Logic changed outside L1 change control
risk.impact: Orders ship without a credit check

threats.title: Reasoning LLM reads "VIP customers may get extended terms" as permission to skip the credit check

risk.failure_mode: Model reinterprets L1 logic; its reasoning trace looks plausible

threats.catalog_note: No entry in /data/threats.json matches this threat. The catalog's model-behavior entries, such as evasion and prompt injection, assume an attacker. Here the model misreads plain business wording and no attacker is involved, so the threat is left unmapped.
threats.notes: Accountable: the AI Model Provider on the provider side (Bill, Nov 17, 2026), the same rule /data/threats.json uses for model-behavior threats. The customer's app team still owns the hard rules in the policy service and the regression tests that catch the change. Contract terms (version pinning, change notice) are an open item.
